clue.text: Bones pong, boy having lost foot

parts.note: a pong is a bad smell, as is a hum in British slang

indicators.note: in a down clue the foot is the last letter, so the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Eric is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A stinking boy, minus a foot, reduced to bones.
explanation.walkthrough: HUM is British slang for a bad smell; ERIC loses its last letter C to give ERI.
explanation.definitionFit: Humeri is the plural of humerus, the long bone of the upper arm.

clue.text: 21 9, formidable competitor with his tools

parts.note: a tiger is a fierce, formidable rival
woods are a type of golf club, the tools of a golfer

explanation.surface: A fearsome rival arrives with his kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is GOLF and 9 is PLAYER, so the definition reads 'golf player'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiger Woods is the famous American golfer, one of the sport's greatest players.

clue.text: Birds pecked others

parts.note: pecked means bit, as a bird does with its beak
the others are other birds, here terns, seabirds

explanation.surface: Some birds attacked their companions with their beaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitterns are wading birds of the heron family, known for their booming call.

clue.text: Anyone's game, as Manx cat and cat back to back

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word for a male cat loses its last letter

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: back says the second cat word is read in reverse

parts.note: puss is a familiar word for a cat

explanation.surface: An open contest is likened to two cats placed back to back.
explanation.walkthrough: TOM without its tail gives TO; PUSS read backwards gives SSUP, placed at the back of the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A toss-up is an even contest whose result is as uncertain as a coin flip.

clue.text: Class 9s performing as per usual?

parts.note: a class or kind is a type
9 across is PLAYER, so 9s are players, collectively a cast

explanation.surface: A group of players do their usual act.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who is typecast keeps being given the same kind of role, so performs as usual.

clue.text: Sculpture capturing heart of nature in work of art, say

indicators.note: capturing says the anagrammed letters hold the central pair of the next word
work of signals that the letters of the following words are worked into a new order
the heart of a word is its central letters

explanation.surface: A sculpture is praised for catching the essence of the natural world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work of' scrambles the two short words into STAARY, which 'capturing' then wraps round the centre of 'nature'; 'in' is only a link, and 'heart of' takes the middle pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Statuary is sculpture collectively, a group of statues.

clue.text: Dancer Jack, in spinning, held high?

indicators.note: spinning turns the two short pieces round so they read backwards

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards
something held high is in the sky

explanation.surface: A dancer called Jack is lifted aloft while twirling.
explanation.walkthrough: J plus IN turned round gives NIJ; 'held high' is IN SKY.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaslav Nijinsky was a celebrated Russian ballet dancer of the Ballets Russes.

clue.text: Athlete took out 9 21

parts.note: to take out someone is to shoot them, so took out means shot
9 is PLAYER and 21 is GOLF: a golf player on the green is a putter

explanation.surface: An athlete eliminated a golfer.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot-putter is a field athlete who hurls a heavy metal ball.

clue.text: Is there no one so hairy but I?

definitions.text: Is there no one so hairy

parts.note: but, in the sense of still or nevertheless, means yet

explanation.surface: A creature asks whether anyone else is as shaggy as itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti is a legendary shaggy ape-like creature said to roam the Himalayas.

clue.text: Participant — in 21!

definitions.meaning: a participant in a game is one who plays
21 is GOLF, and Gary ... is a famous South African golfer

explanation.surface: A competitor is in golf.
explanation.definitionFit: A player takes part in a game, and Gary Player is a golfing great.

clue.text: Swimmer giving bottom a good licking

parts.note: your seat is your bottom
a rout is a heavy defeat, a good licking

explanation.surface: Someone gives another's backside a thorough thrashing.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea trout is a fish, a swimmer in crossword terms.

clue.text: Vegetable pot half gone if reduced

indicators.note: half gone means the last half of the eight-letter pot word is removed

parts.note: a cauldron is a large cooking pot
taken as written
reduced means lowered or made lower

explanation.surface: A cook's vegetable leaves the pot half empty once boiled down.
explanation.walkthrough: CAULDRON loses half its letters to give CAUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Cauliflower is a vegetable of the cabbage family with a white head.

clue.text: Never lie to unreliable 21 9

indicators.note: unreliable suggests the letters of the phrase cannot be trusted to stay in order

explanation.surface: A golfer is warned never to lie to an untrustworthy person.
explanation.definitionFit: Lee Trevino is a Mexican-American golfer with six major titles.

clue.text: But stop here for blue entertainment?

definitions.text: But stop here for blue entertainment?

parts.words: But stop here for blue entertainment?
parts.note: a traffic signal tells you to halt, yet the same words name an area with sex shops and brothels

explanation.surface: A driver halts on the way to an adult show.
explanation.definitionFit: A red light means stop, and a red-light district offers sexual entertainment.

clue.text: Might one rule as queen, embracing old city under me?

indicators.note: in a down clue the rest of the letters sit under the pronoun

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: embracing says the two short words hold the ancient city between them

parts.note: taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the queen
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if they might reign as queen over an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: AS and ER embrace UR to make ASURER, placed below ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule is a measuring stick, so one who measures might use a rule.

clue.text: Odd 21 9

definitions.meaning: 21 is GOLF and 9 is PLAYER: Curtis ... is an American golfer

explanation.surface: An odd golfer.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange means odd, and Curtis Strange won two US Opens at golf.

clue.text: Paper one has to write up for family support

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the whole string is read from the bottom

parts.note: MS, manuscript, is a paper
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
to pen something is to write it

explanation.surface: A newspaper is going to report on support for families.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotism is favouritism shown to relatives, especially in giving jobs.

clue.text: Pornographic sequence filmed away from the studio?

parts.note: OB is outside broadcast, filmed away from the studio
a scene is a filmed sequence

explanation.surface: Explicit footage is shot on location.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene material is indecent, offensive to decency, like pornography.

clue.text: They won't keep his beer pals in order

indicators.note: putting things in order rearranges them, so the letters are sorted into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Someone tells his drinking pals to line up while the beer goes off.
explanation.definitionFit: Perishables are foods that go off quickly and so cannot be kept.

clue.text: A carousing god missing church? You'd count on it!

indicators.note: missing says the church abbreviation is taken out

parts.note: Bacchus is the Roman god of wine and revelry

explanation.surface: A partying deity skips church, which is something to count on.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads used for counting.

clue.text: The way of 21, not not cricket?

definitions.meaning: 21 is GOLF, and the mown stretch towards the green is called the ... way, so this word comes before way
not cricket means unfair, so not not cricket means just and above board

explanation.surface: Golf's path is played by the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: the golf way is the fairway, so the answer is what goes with way.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair means just, and 'not cricket' is a British idiom for unfair.

clue.text: Beat up, hitting in balls with clubs

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word reads from the bottom

parts.note: to flog is to beat

explanation.surface: Someone is thrashed while balls are struck with clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf is a game of hitting balls into holes using clubs.

clue.text: Unsuccessful over holding it right back

indicators.note: holding says the first word contains the reversed pair

parts.note: over means above

indicators.note: back says the two short pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A failed attempt kept the right thing in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the pair to RTI before 'holding' puts it inside; 'over' here is the preposition above, not the cricket over.
explanation.definitionFit: An abortive attempt fails to achieve its end.

clue.text: 21 9 finds the drink round back of green

indicators.note: round means the drink surrounds the letter

parts.note: lager is a drink, beer

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A golfer finds his beer by the far side of the green.
explanation.walkthrough: Bernhard Langer is a German golfer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bernhard Langer is a German golfer, twice winner of the Masters.

clue.text: Saying no to becoming joined together again?

definitions.meaning: fusing is joining; re- means again, so melted together once more

explanation.surface: Refusing to rejoin.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusing means declining, and re-fusing means fusing together again.

clue.text: See 7
